title: AAC Case
description: One test obligation. The normative unit of the AI Assurance Catalog. A case states WHAT must be true, tags WHICH archetypes owe it, and names the CLASS of machinery that can discharge it. A case never names a product, never defines a metric formula, and never sets a threshold.

id.description: Flat, permanent, never reused. Archetype is metadata, not identity — see docs/ID-POLICY.md.

legacy_id.description: Archetype-scoped identifier from draft 0.1 (e.g. A6-01). Retained for traceability only; never cite it in new work.

status.description: Deprecated and superseded cases stay in the catalog forever so citations keep resolving.

since.description: Catalog version in which this case first appeared.

level.description: Obligation strength, RFC 2119 usage, binding only within an adopting organisation.

dimension.description: Quality attribute under test. Must appear in taxonomy/realization.yaml#dimensions.

gate.description: True if failure blocks a release or a request. False means it raises a signal only. This is a property of the obligation, not of any particular deployment — an adopter may still choose to downgrade it in their profile.

archetypes.description: Tags, not a tree. Core cases enumerate every archetype explicitly so a consumer never has to resolve inheritance.

core.description: True if owed by every AI application regardless of shape. Presentational: core cases already list all archetypes.

statement.description: The obligation in plain English. States what must be true and why it matters. Contains no product names, no thresholds, no metric formulas.

mechanisms.description: Advisory. Which classes of machinery can produce a verdict for this obligation.

stages.description: Advisory. Where in the lifecycle this can run.

tool_class.description: Advisory. A CLASS of tool, never a product name. Products belong in realization examples, which are informative and versioned separately.
